name: Woody Johnson

views.text: If the quarterback is holding the team back, I will say so to the coaches, star or not.
A big-name receiver for a big-name quarterback is how you win now.
The decision to change coaches is mine and mine alone.
I let the new coach and general manager make the quarterback call; they report to me.
A slow start is not something I wait out for a whole season.
I want people around the league to see the Jets as a serious contender again.

signatures: is reported to weigh in on lineup and personnel questions
want: A Jets team good enough to end the franchise's long playoff drought (medium).
fear: Being cast as the meddling owner behind another failed era (medium).
voice: Polished and diplomatic in public statements, terse when announcing a decision. Insists decisions are his own. Keeps the rhetoric about winning and the fans.

evidence.summary: Summarizes a report that Johnson suggested benching Aaron Rodgers after a Week 4 loss, drove the Davante Adams trade and pushed other personnel moves, taking control from GM Joe Douglas.
Johnson said the firing of Robert Saleh five games into the season was his decision alone and Rodgers was not consulted.
Head coach Aaron Glenn and GM Darren Mougey each report to Johnson; he said he would leave the Rodgers decision to them.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
